name: Vantablack Media Consensual Blind Relay
description:
The Consensual Blind Relay is a two-party encrypted communication device that functions on a mutual authentication principle — neither party can transmit until both have physically interacted with paired units within a 90-second window. This handshake requirement was originally designed for Vantablack Media's investigative journalism division, where source protection demanded that no communication could be initiated unilaterally or under duress. Each unit generates a one-time cryptographic handshake derived from both users' biometric pressure signatures, creating an encryption key that exists nowhere in either device's memory after the session ends.

The relay itself transmits over a narrow-band compressed audio channel that mimics the acoustic fingerprint of routine data telemetry — the kind of background noise that GLMZ's mesh infrastructure produces constantly. A conversation between two CBR units looks, to any intercepting system, like a malfunctioning environmental sensor reporting ambient temperature data. Vantablack's engineers spent considerable effort ensuring the mimicry layer holds up against the city's more sophisticated traffic analysis algorithms, and the current firmware version has not been successfully de-anonymized in active testing.

Despite its journalistic origins, the Blind Relay has found a far wider audience. Lawyers conducting privileged consultations, corporate defectors arranging handoffs, and couples conducting affairs in surveilled housing blocks all use variants of the same device. Vantablack officially discontinued the consumer line after regulatory pressure, but the schematics leaked within six months and third-party units now outnumber originals three to one on the gray market.

specifications.form_factor: Two paired units, each 8cm x 5cm x 2cm flat card design
specifications.transmission_range: Up to 4km in standard urban mesh density
specifications.session_length: Unlimited within active handshake period; re-authentication required every 6 hours
specifications.traffic_disguise: Environmental telemetry packet mimicry, updated via firmware
specifications.key_retention: Zero — keys purged on session end or unit separation

tactical_use: Primarily used for pre-arranged communications where both parties can confirm physical safety before the channel opens. The mutual activation requirement means the device cannot be used to surveil or trick a contact — both people must consent in real time. Field operatives use them for dead-drop confirmation, source meetings, and exfiltration coordination where one-sided communication would be a liability.
cultural_context: The CBR carries a particular cultural weight in GLMZ's press underground — carrying one is a tacit acknowledgment that you deal in information someone powerful wants suppressed. Among the general population, the device's reputation for absolute discretion has made it a commodity for anyone conducting business they consider private, whether that's labor organizing or infidelity. The original Vantablack-branded units are collector's items among journalists and civil liberties advocates.
story_hooks: A CBR unit is found on a dead informant — its paired unit is still active somewhere in the city, belonging to someone who doesn't yet know their source is gone.
The players receive a CBR unit in the mail with no explanation. Someone wants to meet, but the handshake requires them to show up in person to a location they don't know yet.
A third-party manufactured CBR clone has a subtle flaw in its key disposal — sessions aren't actually being purged. Someone has been quietly archiving conversations for months.

Vantablack Media's legal team is aggressively tracking down the leaked schematics, but the real reason isn't regulatory compliance — the original design contained a hidden channel the engineers never disclosed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A pair of slim, matte black rectangular cards resembling high-end access badges or thin encrypted storage media. Each unit has a subtle convex pressure surface on one face with barely visible micro-dimpling arranged in a 4x6 grid pattern. The opposite face is recessed slightly, creating an almost imperceptible cup — designed to nestle against a palm. No obvious lights or displays; information is minimalist and internal.
physical_description.dimensions: 8cm wide x 5cm tall x 2cm thick per unit; credit-card-thin profile except for a subtle raised spine
physical_description.weight_description: 90g per unit — light enough to pocket, substantial enough to feel intentional in hand; carries weight like a small ceramic tile
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade matte black composite with microstructured grip surface; edges beveled slightly to reduce tactile edges
physical_description.finish: True vantablack-adjacent absorption finish — light seems to die on the surface; minimal reflection even under direct lighting. Grip dimples catch only the faintest highlights
physical_description.color_scheme: Nearly absolute matte black with minimal accent: tiny Neon Arcade Interactive logo in charcoal barely distinguishable on lower spine; hairline etching of paired unit serial numbers visible only at extreme angles
physical_description.interface_elements: Biometric pressure array of 24 contact points across the concave palm-facing surface — individual points unmarked but detectable as slight topographical variations. Ultra-thin connector port (custom, proprietary standard) recessed into bottom edge. No buttons, screens, or LED indicators anywhere on housing
distinctive_features: Grip pressure surface creates 24-point biometric lock — no visual indication of contact points
Vantablack-grade matte finish that absorbs rather than reflects light
Intentionally featureless design — only the pressure geometry hints at function
Paired units must physically touch or be held simultaneously to activate — tactile handshake protocol
Recessed connector port suggests field maintenance but is rarely used
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Neon Arcade Interactive logo (small, charcoal on black) on lower spine; laser-etched unit pairing identifiers (serial pairs); faint regulatory marking (GLMZ compliance stamp) on reverse edge, almost invisible
physical_description.condition_typical: Units are carried in soft pouches or jacket pockets, often with slight scuff marks on edges from repeated pocket carry. Grip dimples may show faint skin oils or wear patterns from heavy use. Serial markings may be deliberately obscured with tape or marker by users in sensitive work

Dramatic side lighting creates imperceptible highlights on the vantablack finish while leaving surfaces largely light-absorbent and mysterious.
